name: Bun ca
summary: Bún cá is fish with rice noodles. Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list makes it a sweet and sour summer bowl of fried tilapia, Vietnamese celery, pineapple, and tomato. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article describes a lunch bowl of fried fish with a green vegetable it compares to morning glory, plus cilantro and dill.
origin: Hanoi. Both descriptions are on Vietnam Tourism. They are not the same bowl.
howToEat: On Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list, rice noodles, Vietnamese celery, and crisp fried tilapia sit in a broth of pineapple and tomato, with herbs and pickled bamboo shoots beside the bowl.
On Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article, the broth is prepared with green vegetables, often a variant of morning glory, and the herbs named are cilantro and dill.
Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list calls it a summer bowl. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article says lunch.
where: Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list points to 14 Trung Yên alley, Hàng Bạc, Hoàn Kiếm. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a second door. The hour is Check on arrival.
seoDescription: Bún cá in Hanoi is fish and rice noodles. One Vietnam Tourism list says tilapia, pineapple, and tomato. Another says fried fish, a morning-glory-like green, cilantro, and dill.
